__NOTE_allowUnsandboxed: false means a command that fails inside the sandbox is NOT retried
with full access, and the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter is
ignored entirely. The agent then reports the blocked host or path
instead of routing around the policy, which is what you want.
__NOTE_failIfUnavailable: If the sandbox itself cannot start, stop rather than running
unconfined. Shown as 'Strict sandbox mode' in the /sandbox Overrides
tab. On Linux and WSL2 the usual cause is a missing socat.

__NOTE_writes: Writes already reach the working directory, a per-user temp
directory, and anything added with --add-dir, /add-dir or
permissions.additionalDirectories. Nothing needs granting here for
the common case of building inside a project.
The base environment is denied explicitly even though no allowWrite
entry includes it, so that a project-level file cannot widen into
it: deny entries merge across scopes and only ever narrow.

__NOTE_credentials: THERE IS NO BUILT-IN DENY LIST. Only the files and variables listed
here are restricted; nothing is protected by default.
A deny entry denies the path for reads inside the sandbox and unsets
the variable before each sandboxed command runs. Deny entries merge
across every settings scope and only ever narrow, so any scope can
add one and no scope can remove one.
